part.name: Symmetric saddle cradle block
part.description: A single-piece rectangular cradle with a concave cylindrical upper bearing surface, a corresponding relieved cylindrical underside, two longitudinal side rails, two raised end cross-members, and a flat underside perimeter rim. No holes, fasteners, or discrete joints are present. Overall STEP bounding box is 2.0 mm wide by 6.0 mm long by 1.5 mm high.
part.symmetry_note: The part is bilaterally symmetric about the STEP x=0 longitudinal center plane and about the y=0 transverse mid-plane. The upper and lower cylindrical surfaces are coaxial with an axis parallel to x, but the part is not symmetric about z=0.

Section.name: Curved saddle web
Section.function intent: Provides the primary shaped interface for supporting or locating a mating cylindrical body while minimizing central material through an underside relief.
Section.physical behavior: The concave upper surface distributes contact load over a broad cylindrical patch. The thin curved web acts as a shell, carrying load primarily through membrane action and bending into the side rails and end cross-members. The approximately coaxial lower relief maintains a near-uniform radial wall thickness.
Section.geometry: A broad concave cylindrical upper patch of radius 4.215 mm and a coaxial lower cylindrical patch of radius 4.415 mm, both generated about the x-axis direction. The upper patch spans x=-1.0 to 1.0 and y=-2.4 to 2.4; the lower patch spans x=-0.8 to 0.8 and approximately y=-2.462 to 2.462.
Section.location: Central region of the part, extending across most of its length between the two raised end cross-members.

major_faces.name: Upper concave saddle surface
major_faces.description: Primary upward-facing cylindrical seating surface, radius 4.215 mm, with its cylinder axis parallel to x.

major_faces.name: Lower cylindrical relief surface
major_faces.description: Downward-facing coaxial cylindrical underside surface, radius 4.415 mm, forming the central relief and curved web thickness.

Section.name: Negative-x side rail
Section.function intent: Stiffens and protects the negative-x edge of the curved web and provides a continuous load path between the two end cross-members.
Section.physical behavior: The spaced outer and inner planar walls form the side of a shallow channel-like shell. This rail resists longitudinal bending, transverse spreading, and local edge deformation while transferring saddle loads toward the underside rim and end cross-members.
Section.geometry: A longitudinal rail bounded by the outer plane at x=-1.0 and the inner cavity plane at x=-0.8. Both faces follow the curved top profile and extend along most of the 6.0 mm part length.
Section.location: Along the negative-x longitudinal edge of the part.

major_faces.name: Negative-x outer side face
major_faces.description: Large external planar side face at x=-1.0, displaying the complete saddle-shaped longitudinal profile.

major_faces.name: Negative-x inner wall
major_faces.description: Planar inner cavity wall at x=-0.8, offset inward from the outer side face to establish the rail thickness.

Section.name: Positive-x side rail
Section.function intent: Stiffens and protects the positive-x edge of the curved web and provides the symmetric load path between the end cross-members.
Section.physical behavior: The outer and inner planar walls act as the side of a shallow channel shell. Together with the opposite rail, this section resists bending and torsion and prevents the saddle web from spreading under contact load.
Section.geometry: A longitudinal rail bounded by the outer plane at x=1.0 and the inner cavity plane at x=0.8. It is the mirror of S02 across x=0.
Section.location: Along the positive-x longitudinal edge of the part.

major_faces.name: Positive-x outer side face
major_faces.description: Large external planar side face at x=1.0, displaying the complete saddle-shaped longitudinal profile.

major_faces.name: Positive-x inner wall
major_faces.description: Planar inner cavity wall at x=0.8, offset inward from the outer side face to establish the rail thickness.

Section.name: Negative-y end cross-member
features included: Axial stop edge for the saddle
Section.function intent: Closes and reinforces the negative-y end of the cradle, provides a flat end landing or interface, and can serve as an axial stop for a mating cylindrical component.
Section.physical behavior: The full-width cross-member ties the two side rails together and resists rail spreading. Its top pad accepts local bearing or clamping load, while the outer and inner end walls transfer that load down to the underside rim.
Section.geometry: A full-width raised block at the negative-y end. It includes an outer top pad at z=0.75, an external wall at y=-3.0, an internal wall at y=-2.8, and a small internal horizontal ledge at z=0.55 connecting toward the lower cylindrical relief.
Section.location: Across the full width at the negative-y end of the part.

major_faces.name: Negative-y external end face
major_faces.description: Full-width external planar end wall at y=-3.0.

major_faces.name: Negative-y upper landing pad
major_faces.description: Flat upper pad at z=0.75 extending from y=-3.0 to the end of the upper cylindrical saddle near y=-2.4.

major_faces.name: Negative-y internal transition ledge
major_faces.description: Small horizontal underside ledge at z=0.55 between the internal end region and lower cylindrical relief.

major_faces.name: Negative-y internal end wall
major_faces.description: Planar cavity-closing wall at y=-2.8 extending between the underside rim and internal upper ledge.

Section.name: Positive-y end cross-member
features included: Axial stop edge for the saddle
Section.function intent: Closes and reinforces the positive-y end of the cradle, provides a second flat landing or interface, and forms the opposing axial stop for a mating component.
Section.physical behavior: The cross-member ties the side rails together, reacts longitudinal and clamping loads, and transfers local pad loads through its end walls to the underside perimeter rim. It mirrors S04 to balance stiffness and loading.
Section.geometry: A full-width raised block at the positive-y end. It includes an outer top pad at z=0.75, an external wall at y=3.0, an internal wall at y=2.8, and a small internal horizontal ledge at z=0.55 adjoining the lower cylindrical relief.
Section.location: Across the full width at the positive-y end of the part.

major_faces.name: Positive-y external end face
major_faces.description: Full-width external planar end wall at y=3.0.

major_faces.name: Positive-y upper landing pad
major_faces.description: Flat upper pad at z=0.75 extending from the end of the upper cylindrical saddle near y=2.4 to y=3.0.

major_faces.name: Positive-y internal transition ledge
major_faces.description: Small horizontal underside ledge at z=0.55 between the lower cylindrical relief and internal end region.

major_faces.name: Positive-y internal end wall
major_faces.description: Planar cavity-closing wall at y=2.8 extending between the underside rim and internal upper ledge.

Section.name: Underside perimeter rim
features included: Opening around the underside relief cavity
Section.function intent: Provides a stable planar base or mounting interface and closes the lower edges of the two rails and two end cross-members while leaving the central relief open.
Section.physical behavior: The continuous planar rim spreads reaction loads around the perimeter, stabilizes the part against rocking, and forms a closed frame that improves torsional rigidity. The central opening reduces mass and preserves clearance beneath the curved web.
Section.geometry: A single planar face at z=-0.75 with two boundary wires: an outer 2.0 mm by 6.0 mm rectangle and an inner opening defining the underside cavity. STEP face area is 3.04 mm squared.
Section.location: Lowest surface of the part, surrounding the central underside cavity.

major_faces.name: Flat underside perimeter rim
major_faces.description: Downward-facing planar annular frame at z=-0.75 surrounding the open underside relief.
